imageAlt: A 3D coral reef on a sandy seabed, with a nurse shark, an octopus, sea urchins and elkhorn coral
summary: Set in Belize waters your guide has explored in person. Tap the creatures, change the conditions, and work out what keeps a reef alive.

lessons.title: Exploring the reef: who lives here, who eats whom, who shelters where

ctaNote: Best on a touchscreen or iPad
audience: Kids, exploring with family, a class, or on their own
objectives: Identify key living and nonliving parts of a reef ecosystem.
Explain how a reef and the habitats next to it give animals food and shelter.
Predict a plausible effect of a change to the ecosystem.
Use evidence from the reef to explain an ecosystem relationship.
access: Runs in your web browser — no install. Best on a touchscreen or iPad.

imageAlt: Earth seen from space, surrounded by hundreds of dots marking satellites in orbit
summary: Fly alongside the satellites that watch our planet. Explore in 3D on a laptop or in a WebXR headset, learn how they work, then solve real scenarios.
firstLesson: How Earth-observation satellites see our planet

imageAlt: A miniature 3D town with a power station, transmission towers, a substation and houses, each part labeled
summary: Start with what electricity actually is, and finish running a whole neighborhood’s grid: balancing supply and demand, and getting the lights back on when things go wrong.
